Harvard School, Los Angeles

Harvard School Commencement Speech哈佛学校毕业典礼演讲

Now that Headmaster Berrisford has selected one of the oldest and longest-serving trustees to make a commencement speech, it behooves the speaker to address two questions in every mind:

既然贝里斯福德（Berrisford）校长在最年长、任职最久的董事中挑出一人来作毕业演讲，那么演讲者就有责任先回答大家心中都有的两个问题：

01Why was such a selection made?
02How long is the speech going to last?

I will answer the first question from long experience alongside Berrisford. He is seeking enhanced reputation for our school in the manner of the man who proudly displays his horse that can count to seven. The man knows that counting to seven is not much of a mathematical feat, but he expects approval because doing so is creditable, considering the performer is a horse.

我对第一个问题的回答，来自我与贝里斯福德共事的长期经验。他正以那个人为榜样，试图为我们学校赢得更高的声誉——那人得意地展示自己的马能数到七。马主人心里清楚，数到七算不上什么数学本事，但他仍期待喝彩，因为考虑到表演者是一匹马，这已堪称难能可贵。

The second question, regarding the length of the speech, I am not going to answer in advance. It would deprive your upturned faces of lively curiosity and obvious keen anticipation, which I prefer to retain, regardless of source.

至于第二个问题，关于演讲的长短，我打算暂时保密。若提前透露，你们仰起的脸庞便会失去那份生动的求知欲和显而易见的殷切期待——无论这份期待源自何处，我都更愿意让它保留下来。

But I will tell you how my consideration of speech length created the subject matter of the speech itself. I was puffed up when invited to speak. While not having significant public speaking experience, I do hold a black belt in chutzpah,71Black belt in chutzpah厚脸皮黑带（厚颜高手） and I immediately considered Demosthenes and Cicero72CiceroA poet, philosopher, rhetorician, and humorist, Marcus Tullius Cicero (106–43 BC) was also one of Rome’s great orators . Cicero viewed public service to be a Roman citizen’s highest duty. He defended those unjustly accused by dictatorial leaders and brought down corrupt governments. Late in life, he led the Senate’s unsuccessful battle against Marc Antony, for which he paid with his life in 43 BC.诗人、哲学家、修辞学家兼幽默作家，马库斯·图利乌斯·西塞罗（Marcus Tullius Cicero，公元前 106–前 43 年）还是罗马最伟大的演说家之一。西塞罗认为，公共服务是罗马公民最高的职责。他为那些被独裁者无端指控的人辩护，并扳倒了腐败的政府。晚年，他领导元老院对抗马克·安东尼（Marc Antony），终究功亏一篑，公元前 43 年为此付出了生命的代价。 as role models and anticipated trying to earn a compliment like Cicero gave when asked which was his favorite among the orations of Demosthenes . Cicero replied, “The longest one.”

不过，我会告诉你们，我正是在思量演讲时长时，想出了本次演讲的主题。接到邀请时，我着实有些飘飘然。虽说缺乏重要的公开演讲经验，但我确有一条黑带的厚脸皮功夫；我立刻把德摩斯梯尼（Demosthenes）和西塞罗71Cicero西塞罗（Cicero）奉为楷模，并盼着能博得西塞罗那句称赞——有人问西塞罗，德摩斯梯尼的演说中最喜欢哪一篇，他答道：“最长那篇。”

However, fortunately for this audience, I also thought of Samuel Johnson’s73Samuel JohnsonSamuel Johnson (1709–1784) , English author and the leading literary scholar and critic of his time, was celebrated for his brilliant and witty conversation. Johnson’s first work of lasting importance, and the one that permanently established his reputation, was his Dictionary of the English Language塞缪尔·约翰逊（Samuel Johnson，1709–1784 年），英国作家，是他那个时代最杰出的文学学者和批评家，以机敏睿智的谈吐闻名。约翰逊第一部具有持久重要性、也永久奠定其声誉的著作，是他的《英语词典》（Dictionary of the English Language）。 famous comment when he addressed Milton’s74John MiltonOne of the greatest poets of the English language, John Milton (1608–1674) was best known for his epic poem Paradise Lost (1667). His powerful prose and the eloquence of his poetry had an immense influence, especially on 18th-century verse. Milton also published pamphlets defending civil and religious rights. To Samuel Johnson’s point about Milton’s long-windedness, Paradise Lost runs to 12 books and thousands of lines.约翰·弥尔顿（John Milton，1608–1674 年）是英语最伟大的诗人之一，以史诗《失乐园》（Paradise Lost，1667 年）最为人知。他有力的散文和诗作的雄辩产生了巨大影响，尤其是对 18 世纪的诗歌。弥尔顿还出版过捍卫公民权利和宗教权利的小册子。就塞缪尔·约翰逊所指出的弥尔顿行文冗长而言，《失乐园》足有 12 卷、数千行。 poem Paradise Lost and correctly said, “No one ever wished it longer.” And that made me consider which of all the 20 Harvard School graduation speeches I had heard that I had wished longer. There was only one such speech, given by Johnny Carson,75Johnny CarsonBorn in Corning, Iowa, Johnny (John William) Carson (1925–2005) became famous as America’s late-night king of comedy. He had a popular radio show in Omaha for years and claimed the city as his hometown. For 30 years, from 1962 to 1992, he entertained millions as the host of NBC’s The Tonight Show . His show featured thousands of authors, filmmakers, actors, singers—and stand-up comedians, of course, many of whose careers he launched.约翰尼·卡森（Johnny Carson，1925–2005 年），全名约翰·威廉·卡森，生于艾奥瓦州科宁，是美国家喻户晓的深夜喜剧之王。他在奥马哈办了多年广受欢迎的广播节目，并把那座城市当作自己的家乡。从 1962 年到 1992 年的 30 年间，他作为 NBC《今夜秀》（The Tonight Show）的主持人娱乐了数百万观众。他的节目迎来了数千位作家、电影人、演员、歌手——当然还有单口喜剧演员，其中许多人的职业生涯都是由他开启的。 specifying Carson’s prescriptions for guaranteed misery in life. I, therefore, decided to repeat Carson’s speech, but in expanded form with some added prescriptions of my own. After all, I am much older than Carson was when he spoke, and I have failed and been miserable more often and in more ways than was possible for a charming humorist speaking at a younger age. I am plainly well qualified to expand on Carson’s theme.

然而，所幸在座诸位，我也想到了塞缪尔·约翰逊73Samuel JohnsonSamuel Johnson (1709–1784) , English author and the leading literary scholar and critic of his time, was celebrated for his brilliant and witty conversation. Johnson’s first work of lasting importance, and the one that permanently established his reputation, was his Dictionary of the English Language塞缪尔·约翰逊（Samuel Johnson，1709–1784 年），英国作家，是他那个时代最杰出的文学学者和批评家，以机敏睿智的谈吐闻名。约翰逊第一部具有持久重要性、也永久奠定其声誉的著作，是他的《英语词典》（Dictionary of the English Language）。（Samuel Johnson）那句名言：他在评弥尔顿74John MiltonOne of the greatest poets of the English language, John Milton (1608–1674) was best known for his epic poem Paradise Lost (1667). His powerful prose and the eloquence of his poetry had an immense influence, especially on 18th-century verse. Milton also published pamphlets defending civil and religious rights. To Samuel Johnson’s point about Milton’s long-windedness, Paradise Lost runs to 12 books and thousands of lines.约翰·弥尔顿（John Milton，1608–1674 年）是英语最伟大的诗人之一，以史诗《失乐园》（Paradise Lost，1667 年）最为人知。他有力的散文和诗作的雄辩产生了巨大影响，尤其是对 18 世纪的诗歌。弥尔顿还出版过捍卫公民权利和宗教权利的小册子。就塞缪尔·约翰逊所指出的弥尔顿行文冗长而言，《失乐园》足有 12 卷、数千行。（Milton）的诗作《失乐园》（Paradise Lost）时，一语中的地说，“从没有人希望它再长些。”这让我回想，自己听过的二十场哈佛学校毕业演讲中，究竟有哪一场曾让我嫌其太短。这样的演讲只有一场，出自约翰尼·卡森75Johnny CarsonBorn in Corning, Iowa, Johnny (John William) Carson (1925–2005) became famous as America’s late-night king of comedy. He had a popular radio show in Omaha for years and claimed the city as his hometown. For 30 years, from 1962 to 1992, he entertained millions as the host of NBC’s The Tonight Show . His show featured thousands of authors, filmmakers, actors, singers—and stand-up comedians, of course, many of whose careers he launched.约翰尼·卡森（Johnny Carson，1925–2005 年），全名约翰·威廉·卡森，生于艾奥瓦州科宁，是美国家喻户晓的深夜喜剧之王。他在奥马哈办了多年广受欢迎的广播节目，并把那座城市当作自己的家乡。从 1962 年到 1992 年的 30 年间，他作为 NBC《今夜秀》（The Tonight Show）的主持人娱乐了数百万观众。他的节目迎来了数千位作家、电影人、演员、歌手——当然还有单口喜剧演员，其中许多人的职业生涯都是由他开启的。（Johnny Carson），他详尽开列了保证人生痛苦的卡森药方。于是我决定复述卡森的演讲，但要加以扩充，再添上几味我自己的药方。毕竟，我比卡森当年演讲时年长得多，失败和受苦的次数更多、方式更杂，远非一位年轻风趣的幽默家所能比拟。显然，我有充分资格把卡森的主题发扬光大。

What Carson said was that he couldn’t tell the graduating class how to be happy, but he could tell them from personal experience how to guarantee misery. Carson’s prescription for sure misery included:

卡森的原话是，他无法告诉毕业班的同学怎样才能幸福，却可以根据切身经验告诉他们，如何保证自己痛苦一生。卡森确保痛苦的处方包括：

01Ingesting chemicals in an effort to alter mood or perception
02Envy
03Resentment
“Carson said he couldn’t tell the graduating class how to be happy, but he could tell them from personal experience how to guarantee misery.”卡森（Carson）说，他没法告诉毕业班怎么获得幸福，但他能以自己的亲身经历告诉他们，怎么确保得到痛苦。

I can still recall Carson’s absolute conviction as he told how he had tried these things on occasion after occasion and had become miserable every time.

我至今仍能想起卡森那不容置疑的神情：他讲述自己一次次地试过这些法子，而每一次都变得痛苦不堪。

It is easy to understand Carson’s first prescription for misery, ingesting chemicals. I add my voice. The four closest friends of my youth were highly intelligent, ethical, humorous types, favored in person and background. Two are long dead, with alcohol a contributing factor, and a third is a living alcoholic—if you call that living.

卡森第一味痛苦药方——摄入化学物质——其道理不难理解。我也来添几句。我年轻时最要好的四个朋友，都聪慧、正派、风趣，自身条件与家庭背景皆属上乘。其中两位早已离世，酒精难辞其咎；第三位虽还活着，却是个酒鬼——假如那也算活着的话。

While susceptibility varies, addiction can happen to any of us through a subtle process where the bonds of degradation are too light to be felt until they are too strong to be broken. And yet, I have yet to meet anyone, in over six decades of life, whose life was worsened by fear and avoidance of such a deceptive pathway to destruction.

虽说易感程度因人而异，但任何人都有可能经由一个微妙的过程染上毒瘾：堕落之索起初轻得让人毫无察觉，待到沉重得无法挣脱时方才醒悟。然而，在我六十余载的人生里，却从未遇见哪个人，因为对这条通往毁灭的欺人之途心怀畏惧、敬而远之，而令自己的生活变得更糟。

Envy, of course, joins chemicals in winning some sort of quantity prize for causing misery. It was wreaking havoc long before it got bad press in the laws of Moses.76The Laws of Moses摩西律法 If you wish to retain the contribution of envy to misery, I recommend that you never read any of the biographies of that good Christian Samuel Johnson, because his life demonstrates in an enticing way the possibility and advantage of transcending envy.

妒忌自然与化学物质一样，能在制造痛苦方面争得某种数量级的奖项。早在摩西（Moses）的律法给它恶名之前，它便已酿成无穷祸患。若你愿让妒忌继续为痛苦效力，我劝你千万别去读那位虔诚信徒塞缪尔·约翰逊的任何传记，因为他的一生以诱人的方式，展示了超越妒忌的可能与益处。

Resentment has always worked for me exactly as it worked for Carson. I cannot recommend it highly enough to you if you desire misery. Johnson spoke well when he said that life is hard enough to swallow without squeezing in the bitter rind of resentment.

怨恨之于我，向来如同之于卡森一般奏效。若你渴望痛苦，我实在找不到比它更值得力荐的药方。约翰逊说得妙：人生本已艰涩难咽，何必再把怨恨的苦皮硬塞进去。

约翰逊说得妙：人生本已艰涩难咽，何必再把怨恨的苦皮硬塞进去。

Samuel Johnson
“Johnson spoke well when he said that life is hard enough to swallow without squeezing in the bitter rind of resentment.”约翰逊（Johnson）有句话说得好：人生本已够难下咽，何必再塞进怨恨的苦皮。

For those of you who want misery, I also recommend refraining from the practice of the Disraeli compromise, designed for people who find it impossible to quit resentment cold turkey. Benjamin Disraeli,78Benjamin Disraeli本杰明·迪斯雷利 as he rose to become one of the greatest prime ministers, learned to give up vengeance as a motivation for action, but he did retain some outlet for resentment by putting the names of people who wronged him on pieces of paper in a drawer. Then, from time to time, he reviewed these names and took pleasure in noting the way the world had taken his enemies down without his assistance.

你们这些一心求苦的人，我还建议你们切勿效仿狄斯雷利（Disraeli）的折中之计——那是专为那些无法对怨恨“一刀切”的人设计的。狄斯雷利在跻身最伟大的首相之列的过程中，学会了不再把复仇当作行动的动力，却仍给怨恨留了出口：他把那些辜负过自己的人的名字写在纸条上，塞进抽屉。然后不时翻看这些名字，欣然记下这个世界如何无须他插手，便将他的敌人一一扳倒。

Well, so much for Carson’s three prescriptions. Here are four more prescriptions from Munger:

好，卡森的三味药方便说这些。下面再献上四味芒格（Munger）的药方：

First, be unreliable. Do not faithfully do what you have engaged to do. If you will only master this one habit, you will more than counterbalance the combined effect of all your virtues, howsoever great. If you like being distrusted and excluded from the best human contribution and company, this prescription is for you. Master this one habit, and you will always play the role of the hare in the fable, except that instead of being outrun by one fine turtle, you will be outrun by hordes and hordes of mediocre turtles, and even some mediocre turtles on crutches.

第一，不可靠。不要忠实履行你承诺过的事。只要你能练成这一种习惯，便足以抵消你全部美德合起来的效用，无论那些美德多么伟大。若你喜欢被人猜疑、被排斥在最优的人类贡献与交游之外，这味药方正合你用。练成这一种习惯，你便永远扮演寓言里那只兔子，只不过击败你的不再是一只出色的乌龟，而是一群又一群平庸的乌龟，甚至还包括几只拄着拐杖的平庸乌龟。

I must warn you that if you don’t follow my first prescription, it may be hard to end up miserable even if you start disadvantaged. I had a roommate in college who was and is severely dyslexic. But he is perhaps the most reliable man I have ever known. He has had a wonderful life so far: an outstanding wife and children, chief executive of a multibillion-dollar corporation. If you want to avoid a conventional, main-culture, establishment result of this kind, you simply can’t count on your other handicaps to hold you back if you persist in being reliable.

我必须提醒你们，若不照我的第一味药方行事，即便你起步处于劣势，也未必能落得痛苦下场。我大学时有个室友，当时乃至如今都患有严重的阅读障碍。但他或许是我所识最可靠的人。他迄今为止人生美满：妻子儿女出众，执掌着一家市值数十亿美元的企业。若你想避开这类传统、主流、建制化的成就，却又执意做个可靠的人，那么光靠你其他的缺陷，可拦不住你。

I cannot here pass by a reference to a life described as “wonderful so far” without reinforcing the “so far” aspects of the human condition by repeating the remark of Croesus,79Croesus(c. 620–546 BC), legendary for his huge wealth, was king of Lydia from 585 BC until his defeat by the Persians in about 546 BC. Upon capture, Croesus supposedly threw himself upon a funeral pyre.克罗伊斯（Croesus，约公元前 620–前 546 年）以巨额财富闻名，自公元前 585 年起为吕底亚国王，直到约公元前 546 年被波斯人击败。据说被俘后，克罗伊斯投身于柴堆自焚。 once the richest king in the world. Later, in ignominious captivity, as he prepared to be burned alive, he said, “Well now do I remember the words of the historian Solon: ‘No man’s life should be accounted a happy one until it is over.’”

我在此提及一段被形容为“迄今为止美满”的人生，不能不借克洛伊斯（Croesus）的话，来强化人类处境中那“迄今为止”的一面——克洛伊斯曾是世界上最富有的国王。后来，在受辱为囚、即将被活活烧死之际，他说：“此刻我才想起史家梭伦（Solon）的那句话：‘人的一生，未到终了，不可言幸福。’”

My second prescription for misery is to learn everything you possibly can from your own experience, minimizing what you learn vicariously from the good and bad experiences of others, living and dead. This prescription is a sure-shot producer of misery and second-rate achievement.

我开给你的第二味痛苦药方是：竭力学尽你自身体验中所能学到的一切，而尽量不去从他人——无论生死——的成败得失中旁敲侧击地吸收教训。这味药方必能让你痛苦缠身、成就平平。

You can see the results of not learning from others’ mistakes by simply looking about you. How little originality there is in the common disasters of mankind: drunk driving deaths, reckless driving maimings, incurable venereal diseases, conversion of bright college students into brainwashed zombies as members of destructive cults, business failures through repetition of obvious mistakes made by predecessors, various forms of crowd folly, and so on. I recommend as a memory clue to finding the way to real trouble from heedless, unoriginal error the modern saying “If at first you don’t succeed, well, so much for hang gliding.”

只要环顾四周，你便能看出不向他人错误学习的结果。人类常见的灾祸竟是那般缺乏创意：酒驾致死、鲁莽驾驶致残、不治的性病、聪明的大学生加入毁灭性邪教后被洗脑成行尸走肉、因重蹈前人显而易见的覆辙而破产、形形色色的群体愚行，不一而足。我建议你们记住一句现代俗语，作为从草率而毫无新意的错误中走向真正麻烦的记路标：“若起初未获成功，啊，悬挂式滑翔就此别过。”

“若起初未获成功，啊，悬挂式滑翔就此别过。”

“If at first you don’t succeed, well, so much for hangxa0gliding.”假如起初你不成功，那么，滑翔伞这事就算了吧。

The other aspect of avoiding vicarious wisdom is the rule of not learning from the best work done before yours. The prescription is to become as non-educated as you reasonably can.

避开他人智慧的另一方面，是那条不向前人最优成果学习的规矩。这味药方，就是尽量让自己所受的教育少得可怜。

Perhaps you will better see the type of non-miserable result you can thus avoid if I render a short historical account. There once was a man who assiduously mastered the work of his best predecessors, despite a poor start and very tough time in analytical geometry. Eventually, his own work attracted wide attention, and he said of his work, “If I have seen a little farther than other men, it is because I stood on the shoulders of giants.” The bones of that man lie buried now, in Westminster Abbey, under an unusual inscription: “Here lie the remains of all that was mortal in Sir Isaac Newton.”80Isaac NewtonAt birth in Lincolnshire, England, Isaac Newton (1642–1727) was so tiny and frail that he was not expected to live. Yet he lived into his 80s. During his young adulthood, Newton made tremendous discoveries in general mathematics, algebra, geometry, calculus, optics, and celestial mechanics. Most famous among these discoveries was his description of gravity. The publication of his book The Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy in 1687 marked the peak of Newton’s creative career.艾萨克·牛顿（Isaac Newton，1642–1727 年）生于英格兰林肯郡，出生时瘦小孱弱，人们以为他活不下来。然而他一直活到八十多岁。青年时期，牛顿在普通数学、代数、几何、微积分、光学和天体力学上都取得了巨大发现，其中最著名的是他对万有引力的描述。1687 年他的著作《自然哲学的数学原理》（The Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy）出版，标志着他创造生涯的巅峰。

若我讲一段简短的史实，你或许更能看清，你能借此避开的，是怎样一种不痛苦的下场。从前有个人，尽管起步不佳、在解析几何上吃尽苦头，却仍勤勉地掌握了前人最卓越的成就。最终，他自己的研究引来广泛关注，他如此评价自己的工作：“若我比旁人看得稍远一些，那是因为我站在巨人的肩上。”此人遗骨今葬于威斯敏斯特教堂（Westminster Abbey），墓碑上刻着一句异乎寻常的铭文：“此处长眠着艾萨克·牛顿80Isaac NewtonAt birth in Lincolnshire, England, Isaac Newton (1642–1727) was so tiny and frail that he was not expected to live. Yet he lived into his 80s. During his young adulthood, Newton made tremendous discoveries in general mathematics, algebra, geometry, calculus, optics, and celestial mechanics. Most famous among these discoveries was his description of gravity. The publication of his book The Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy in 1687 marked the peak of Newton’s creative career.艾萨克·牛顿（Isaac Newton，1642–1727 年）生于英格兰林肯郡，出生时瘦小孱弱，人们以为他活不下来。然而他一直活到八十多岁。青年时期，牛顿在普通数学、代数、几何、微积分、光学和天体力学上都取得了巨大发现，其中最著名的是他对万有引力的描述。1687 年他的著作《自然哲学的数学原理》（The Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy）出版，标志着他创造生涯的巅峰。（Isaac Newton）爵士一切终有一死的部分。”

My third prescription to you for misery is to go down and stay down when you get your first, second, or third severe reverse in the battle of life. Because there is so much adversity out there, even for the lucky and wise, this will guarantee that, in due course, you will be permanently mired in misery. Ignore at all cost the lesson contained in the accurate epitaph written for himself by Epictetus:81EpictetusEven though he was born a slave in Hierapolis and endured a permanent physical disability, (55–135) maintained that all human beings are perfectly free to control their own lives and to live in harmony with nature. After intense study of the traditional Stoic curriculum of logic, physics, and ethics, Epictetus spent his entire career teaching philosophy and promoting a daily regime of rigorous self-examination. He eventually gained his freedom but was exiled from Rome by Domitian in 89.爱比克泰德（Epictetus，55–135 年）虽生于希拉波利斯、身为奴隶，且身有终身残疾，却主张所有人都完全有自由掌控自己的生活、与自然和谐共处。在深入研习逻辑学、物理学和伦理学的传统斯多葛课程之后，爱比克泰德毕生致力于教授哲学，并倡导每日严格自省的习惯。他最终获得了自由，却在公元 89 年被多米提安（Domitian）逐出罗马。 “Here lies Epictetus, a slave, maimed in body, the ultimate in poverty, and favored by the gods.”

我开给你的第三味痛苦药方是：当你在人生战场上遭遇第一、第二或第三次重挫时，便一蹶不振、就此躺平。外面的逆境如此之多，即便对幸运而睿智之人亦然，这味药方必能保你在适当的时辰，永远陷在痛苦的泥沼里。务请不惜一切代价，忽略爱比克泰德81EpictetusEven though he was born a slave in Hierapolis and endured a permanent physical disability, (55–135) maintained that all human beings are perfectly free to control their own lives and to live in harmony with nature. After intense study of the traditional Stoic curriculum of logic, physics, and ethics, Epictetus spent his entire career teaching philosophy and promoting a daily regime of rigorous self-examination. He eventually gained his freedom but was exiled from Rome by Domitian in 89.爱比克泰德（Epictetus，55–135 年）虽生于希拉波利斯、身为奴隶，且身有终身残疾，却主张所有人都完全有自由掌控自己的生活、与自然和谐共处。在深入研习逻辑学、物理学和伦理学的传统斯多葛课程之后，爱比克泰德毕生致力于教授哲学，并倡导每日严格自省的习惯。他最终获得了自由，却在公元 89 年被多米提安（Domitian）逐出罗马。（Epictetus）自撰的那句贴切墓志铭中所藏的教训：“此处长眠着爱比克泰德，一介奴隶，身有残缺，赤贫至极，却蒙神恩宠。”

My final prescription to you for a life of fuzzy thinking and infelicity is to ignore a story they told me when I was very young about a rustic who said, “I wish I knew where I was going to die, and then I’d never go there.” Most people smile, as you did, at the rustic’s ignorance and ignore his basic wisdom. If my experience is any guide, the rustic’s approach is to be avoided at all cost by someone bent on misery. To help fail, you should discount as mere quirk, with no useful message, the method of the rustic, which is the same one used in Carson’s speech.

我开给你的最后一味药方，通向糊里糊涂、郁郁寡欢的一生：忽略我幼时听人讲过的那个乡下人的故事。他说：“但愿我知道自己会死在哪儿，那样我就永远不去那个地方。”大多数人都会像你们方才那样，冲着乡下人的无知一笑置之，忽略他朴素的智慧。以我的经验而论，那个一心求苦的人，无论如何都要避开这乡下人的法子。要想失败得漂亮，你该把乡下人的方法——亦即卡森演讲所用的方法——贬作毫无裨益的怪癖，不值一顾。

What Carson did was to approach the study of how to create X by turning the question backward—that is, by studying how to create non-X. The great algebraist Jacobi82Carl Jacobi卡尔·雅可比 had exactly the same approach as Carson and was known for his constant repetition of one phrase: “Invert, always invert.”83Invert, always invert反过来想，总是反过来想 It is in the nature of things, as Jacobi knew, that many hard problems are best solved only when they are addressed backward. “Many hard problems are best solved when they are addressed backward.”许多难题，倒着想解决最好。

It is my opinion, as a certified biography nut, that Charles Robert Darwin86Charles DarwinCharles Darwin (1809–1882) was a British naturalist whose teachings on evolution by natural selection revolutionized the science of biology. His book On the Origin of Species sold out immediately and was heavily attacked because it did not support the depiction of creation given in the Bible.查尔斯·达尔文（Charles Darwin，1809–1882 年）是英国博物学家，他关于自然选择进化的学说彻底改变了生物学。他的著作《物种起源》（On the Origin of Species）甫一出版即售罄，却因不支持《圣经》所描述的创世而遭到猛烈抨击。 would have ranked near the middle of the Harvard School graduating class of 1986. Yet he is now famous in the history of science. This is precisely the type of example you should learn nothing from if bent on minimizing your results from your own endowment.

作为一名货真价实的传记迷，我以为，查尔斯·罗伯特·达尔文86Charles DarwinCharles Darwin (1809–1882) was a British naturalist whose teachings on evolution by natural selection revolutionized the science of biology. His book On the Origin of Species sold out immediately and was heavily attacked because it did not support the depiction of creation given in the Bible.查尔斯·达尔文（Charles Darwin，1809–1882 年）是英国博物学家，他关于自然选择进化的学说彻底改变了生物学。他的著作《物种起源》（On the Origin of Species）甫一出版即售罄，却因不支持《圣经》所描述的创世而遭到猛烈抨击。（Charles Robert Darwin）若置身哈佛学校1986届毕业班，成绩大概只在中游。然而他如今已是科学史上的巨擘。若你执意要让自己天赋的果实缩到最小，这恰恰是你不该从中吸取教训的样板。

Darwin’s result was due in large measure to his working method, which violated all my rules for misery and particularly emphasized a backward twist in that he always gave priority attention to evidence tending to disconfirm whatever cherished and hard-won theory he already had. In contrast, most people early achieve and later intensify a tendency to process new and disconfirming information so that any original conclusion remains intact. They become people of whom Philip Wylie87Philip Wylie菲利普·怀利 observed, “You couldn’t squeeze a dime between what they already know and what they will never learn.”

达尔文的成就，大半得自他的工作方法——它违背了我所有关于痛苦的规则，尤其强调一种逆向的扭转：他总把最优先的注意力，放在那些倾向于推翻他既有的、珍视的、得来不易的理论的证据上。相形之下，大多数人早早养成一种倾向，后来又不断强化：他们处理新的、证伪性的信息时，总要让最初的结论完好无损。他们变成了菲利普·威利（Philip Wylie）所形容的那种人：“在他们已知之事与他们永不会学之事之间，你连一枚一角硬币都塞不进去。”

The life of Darwin demonstrates how a turtle may outrun a hare, aided by extreme objectivity, which helps the objective person end up like the only player without a blindfold in a game of pin the tail on the donkey.88Pin the tail on the donkey给驴子贴尾巴（蒙眼游戏）

达尔文的一生昭示了：一只乌龟，借助极致的客观，如何能够跑赢兔子——这种客观，能让客观之人最终像“给驴子贴尾巴”游戏中唯一没被蒙住眼睛的玩家。

“达尔文的一生昭示了：一只乌龟，借助极致的客观，如何能够跑赢兔子。”

“The life of Darwin demonstrates how a turtle may outrun a hare, aided by extremexa0objectivity.”达尔文的一生说明：一只乌龟如何藉由极度的客观，跑赢了兔子。

If you minimize objectivity, you ignore not only a lesson from Darwin but also one from Einstein. Einstein said that his successful theories came from “curiosity, concentration, perseverance, and self-criticism.” And by self-criticism, he meant the testing and destruction of his own well-loved ideas.

若你弱化客观，你忽略的便不只是达尔文的教训，还有爱因斯坦的。爱因斯坦说，他那些成功的理论源自“好奇、专注、坚毅与自省”。而他所说的自省，指的是检验并推翻他自己深爱的想法。

Finally, minimizing objectivity will help you lessen the compromises and burden of owning worldly goods, because objectivity does not work only for great physicists and biologists. It also adds power to the work of a plumbing contractor89Plumbing contractor管道承包商 in Bemidji. Therefore, if you interpret being true to yourself as requiring that you retain every notion of your youth, you will be safely underway, not only toward maximizing ignorance but also toward whatever misery can be obtained through unpleasant experiences in business.

最后，弱化客观还将帮你减轻拥有世俗财物的妥协与负担，因为客观之道并非只为伟大的物理学家与生物学家而设。它同样能给伯米吉（Bemidji）一位管道工的工作增添力量。故此，若你把“忠实于自己”理解为必须保留年少时的每一个念头，那你便稳妥地上路了——不仅朝最大化无知的方向，也朝生意场上种种不快经历所能带来的痛苦一路疾行。

It is fitting that a backward sort of speech end with a backward sort of toast, inspired by Elihu Root’s90Elihu RootElihu Root (1845–1937) , born in New York and the son of a mathematics professor, became one of the most brilliant administrators in American history. By age 30, he had established himself as a prominent lawyer specializing in corporate affairs. Shifting to public service, Root distinguished himself as secretary of war, secretary of state, US senator, and ambassador to Russia. In the interest of worldwide peace, he originated many treaties of arbitration. He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1912.伊莱休·鲁特（Elihu Root，1845–1937 年）生于纽约，是一位数学教授之子，后来成为美国历史上最杰出的行政管理者之一。30 岁时，他已是一名专攻公司事务的知名律师。转向公共服务后，鲁特先后以陆军部长、国务卿、联邦参议员和驻俄大使的身份崭露头角。出于对世界和平的关注，他首创了许多仲裁条约。1912 年，他被授予诺贝尔和平奖。 repeated accounts of how the dog went to Dover, “leg over leg.”91How the dog went to Dover小狗如何去了多佛 To the class of 1986: Gentlemen, may each of you rise by spending each day of a long life aiming low.
